# MSGraphPermissions Documentation

This folder contains the Markdown documentation for the MSGraphPermissions PowerShell module, generated using [PlatyPS](https://github.com/PowerShell/platyPS).

## Automatic Updates

**Documentation is automatically generated and updated by CI/CD workflows!**

When you:
- Push changes to a pull request
- Merge to main/master branch

The GitHub Actions workflow will:
1. Build documentation from your comment-based help
2. Commit any changes back to the branch automatically
3. Keep docs synchronized with code

**You don't need to manually run any commands!** Just update your function's comment-based help in the code, and CI handles the rest.

## Manual Documentation Build (Optional)

If you want to preview documentation locally before pushing:

```powershell
# Generate/update markdown from code
.\build\Build-Documentation.ps1 -UpdateMarkdown

# Test the help
Import-Module .\MSGraphPermissions\MSGraphPermissions.psd1 -Force
Get-Help Find-GraphLeastPrivilege -Full
```

## Manual Enhancements

You can manually edit the Markdown files in this folder to:
- Add more detailed descriptions
- Improve examples with better output samples
- Add additional notes and warnings
- Include links to Microsoft documentation
- Format code blocks

**Note:** Manual edits will be preserved when CI updates documentation, as long as you don't modify the auto-generated sections (SYNOPSIS, SYNTAX, PARAMETERS).

## Files

- **MSGraphPermissions.md** - Module overview page
- **[CommandName].md** - Individual command help files
- Each file corresponds to an exported function

## Testing

Test the generated help:
```powershell
Import-Module .\MSGraphPermissions\MSGraphPermissions.psd1 -Force
Get-Help Find-GraphLeastPrivilege -Full
Get-Help Find-GraphPath -Examples
```

## Build Process

The `Build-Documentation.ps1` script (run automatically by CI):
1. Exports Markdown from comment-based help in your functions
2. Compiles Markdown to MAML (XML help files)
3. Places MAML in `MSGraphPermissions\en-US\` for `Get-Help` system
4. Validates documentation for issues
5. CI commits any changes back to your branch

## CI/CD Integration

### Pull Request Workflow
1. You update function code and comment-based help
2. Push to PR branch
3. CI builds docs and commits changes to your PR automatically
4. You can review the auto-committed documentation changes
5. Merge when ready

### Main Branch Workflow
1. PR merged to main/master
2. CI rebuilds docs to ensure they're current
3. Auto-commits any updates
4. Module is validated and published

## Notes

- Markdown files are version controlled and auto-updated
- MAML files (`.xml`) are auto-generated by CI
- Just update comment-based help in your `.ps1` files - CI does the rest
- Manual Markdown enhancements are preserved during updates
